root_idea.summary: The root centers on orphanhood as separation from one's originating parent and extends lexically to the condition of standing alone or being peerless.
root_idea.development: In human usage, orphanhood is loss of the father before maturity; in animals, it is loss of the mother. The same idea of separation and singularity can extend to any solitary or unmatched thing. The Qur'anic form represents the human branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The QAC group is represented under the normalized singular citation form يَتِيم, covering its singular and plural Quranic inflections.

senses.definition: A child deprived of his or her father before reaching maturity; an orphan.
senses.usage_conditions: The Qur'anic form includes the singular يَتِيم and the plural يَتَامَى, used substantivally and adjectivally for human orphans.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone fatherless; to cause someone to become an orphan.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV verb describing the causative action of making a person an orphan.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A solitary or peerless thing, such as a unique pearl; by extension, an exceptional or singular poetic verse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader figurative use based on being separated from one's source or having no equal; this is not the human-orphan sense represented by the Qur'anic occurrences.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit explicitly defines the Form IV causative verb as making someone fatherless.

cautions: The QAC group combines singular يَتِيم and plural يَتَامَى forms with noun and adjective analyses; the public headword is the singular dictionary citation form.
